before.approach: From Glacier, WA, drive Mt. Baker Highway (SR 542) east about 1 mile past the Glacier Public Service Center to Glacier Creek Road (FS 39); turn right, then take an immediate left onto Deadhorse Road (FS 37). FS 37 normally continues 12.7 miles to the Skyline Divide Trailhead. As of the Forest Service's current alert, FS 37 is impassable at milepost 3.1 due to 2021 flood damage with no estimated repair date, so the trailhead is not currently reachable by vehicle. When open, hike Skyline Divide Trail #678 through old-growth forest switchbacks and into meadows (~4.4–4.5 mi) to the ridge crest, then continue cross-country along the open ridge to Chowder Ridge and the base of Hadley Peak.
watch_out: As of the current Forest Service alert, FS Road 37 is washed out at milepost 3.1 with no repair date, making the Skyline Divide Trailhead inaccessible by vehicle — check current Forest Service alerts before planning this approach.
Loose scree and talus on the final summit push; a short Class 3 step near the top has real exposure.
Snow can linger on the ridge into July, requiring an ice axe and self-arrest skill on the traverse.

approach_variants.name: Skyline Divide Trail #678 and the long open ridge east to Chowder Ridge
approach_variants.notes:
ACCESS FIRST: from Glacier, WA drive SR-542 about a mile past the Glacier Public Service Center to Glacier Creek Road (FS-39), turn right, then immediately left onto Deadhorse Road (FS-37). FS-37 normally runs 12.7 miles to the Skyline Divide trailhead. Under the Forest Service's current alert FS-37 is impassable at milepost 3.1 from 2021 flood damage with no estimated repair date, so the trailhead is not reachable by vehicle. Confirm before planning around it.

When open, Skyline Divide Trail #678 climbs through old-growth switchbacks into meadows and reaches the ridge crest at about 4.4-4.5 miles. From there the route is cross-country along the open ridge — roughly three miles of it — to Chowder Ridge and the base of Hadley's summit block.

The first viewpoint on the crest near 6,600 ft is the landmark parties use to re-find the maintained trail on the way back.
approach_variants.season: Roughly Aug-Oct — this trailhead may not currently be reachable at all
hazards: FS-37 impassable at milepost 3.1 with no repair date — the trailhead may not be drivable at all
Three miles of cross-country open ridge with no tread and no cairns
A short Class 3 step above loose scree and talus
Two unmarked divides converging on one summit, with very different roads at the bottom
No water once past the meadows
approach_variants.baseFinding:
THE 6,600 FT VIEWPOINT IS THE GATE, IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. It is where maintained trail ends and where you rejoin it. In cloud it is the only reliable waypoint on this approach, because everything east of it is three miles of undifferentiated open ridge. Note it on the way out — parties who do not, spend the return walking a crest that all looks the same.

THE CREST IS THE HANDRAIL. From the viewpoint the route runs EAST along the ridge for roughly three miles to Chowder Ridge. Keep the crest under your feet with air on both sides; this ridge has heather benches falling away either side and it is easy to drift onto one and lose the line.

ARRIVAL AT THE CLIMBING: the summit block is a SHORT CLASS 3 STEP above loose scree and talus — the last stretch of the day and the only scrambling on it. Walking stops, one short step of rock, summit. That is the whole climb, and it is the test: if you are scrambling for a long time, you are on a false feature; if you have not left your feet, you are not there.

THE DISCRIMINATOR AGAINST THE OTHER APPROACH TO THIS SAME BLOCK: Cougar Divide arrives on Chowder Ridge from the NORTH-WEST after crossing near Dobbs Creek, and its trail high point is 5,920 ft. Skyline arrives from the WEST after roughly three miles of ridge from a 6,600 ft viewpoint. If you are descending in poor visibility, going down the wrong divide puts you 11 miles of gravel road away from your car on a road that may itself be washed out.

road.name: Deadhorse Road (Forest Service Road 37)
road.status: Closed to vehicles at mile 0.03 until further notice while flood-damage repair is under way, per the Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie alert of 1 June 2026
road.driveNote: From Glacier, drive SR 542 east about 1 mile, turn right onto Glacier Creek Road (FS 39), then take an immediate left onto Deadhorse Road (FS 37); FS 37 normally continues 12.7 miles to the Skyline Divide Trailhead, but is currently gated at mile 0.03 for repair work.
road.seasonalGate: No routine seasonal gate reported for FS 37 itself; access is presently blocked by the unrepaired washout regardless of season

climate.fall: Often clear and dry with fewer bugs, but shorter daylight and increasing chance of early-season snow by October.
climate.spring: Ridge typically still snow-covered; not the standard scramble season.
climate.summer: Prime season (July-September); trail generally snow-free by July, though the ridge traverse can hold patchy snow into early July.
climate.winter: Full winter mountaineering/avalanche conditions; not the standard scramble route in winter.
climate.typical: Wet, maritime North Cascades weather with rapid changes possible even in summer; the exposed ridge crest is prone to wind and fast-moving cloud.
climate.forecastZone: NWAC West Slopes North (Mount Baker area)

before.beta: From the Skyline Divide Trailhead, a rugged, eroded trail switchbacks through forest and into alpine meadows for about 4.4–4.5 miles to the first ridge-crest viewpoint (~6,600 ft). From there the maintained tread fades into a boot-packed path that continues along the open ridge crest for roughly another 3 miles, crossing minor ups and downs on Chowder Ridge, before reaching the base of Hadley Peak's final scramble. The last push is Class 2 with a short Class 3 step, climbing loose scree and talus to the summit; exposure is generally minimal for experienced parties.

pitch_detail.notes: Trailhead through forest to Skyline Divide meadows (Trail #678), ~2 miles
Along Skyline Divide ridge crest to ~6,563 ft, ~1.5 miles of established trail
Cross-country north along the ridge to the Chowder Ridge junction
Chowder Ridge traverse on an established boot-path; mild exposure, side-hilling on steep slope
Final northwest-ridge summit block; loose rock, hard class 3 scrambling to the small, exposed summit

before.descent_text: From the summit, carefully downclimb the short Class 3 step and the loose scree/talus below it back to the base of the summit block. Retrace the boot-packed path along Chowder Ridge and the open ridge crest (roughly 3 miles) back to the first viewpoint (~6,600 ft), then descend the maintained Skyline Divide Trail #678 through meadows and forest switchbacks to the trailhead.

access.fees: $5/vehicle day-use fee at the trailhead, or annual Recreation/Interagency Pass
access.rules: Pack out human waste (blue bags) — no burial or glacier deposition. Some approaches cross into North Cascades National Park land on the upper mountain, where a free NPS backcountry permit is required only if camping overnight past the boundary.
access.permit: Free self-issue wilderness permit available at the trailhead
access.closures: Skyline Divide Trailhead is currently inaccessible by vehicle: FS Road 37 (Deadhorse Road) is closed at mile 0.03 until further notice for flood-damage repair, with heavy equipment on the road.
access.landManager: USDA Forest Service, Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest (Mount Baker Wilderness)
access.land_manager: Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest (Mt. Baker Ranger District) — Mount Baker Wilderness, with some upper routes crossing into North Cascades National Park
access.parking_pass: Northwest Forest Pass required at most trailheads — $30/year or $5/day.
access.passRequired: Northwest Forest Pass or other accepted Interagency Pass

overnight_permit.where: No climbing or wilderness permit. A recreation pass is needed to park at the Heliotrope Ridge and Park Butte trailheads; buy it ahead or on the Recreation.gov app.

before.approach: From Glacier, WA, drive Mt. Baker Highway (SR 542) east and turn onto Forest Service Road 33; follow roughly 11 miles of gravel road (rough in sections, high-clearance/SUV recommended, sedans passable with care) to its end at the Cougar Divide Trailhead/parking (room for 8-10 vehicles). Note the true trailhead may be roughly another kilometer past where online mapping apps route. Hike Cougar Divide Trail #601 along the ridge to its high point (~5,920 ft), then continue cross-country northeast along the open ridge, crossing near Dobbs Creek, to Chowder Ridge and the base of Hadley Peak's final scramble.

pitch_detail.notes: Trailhead through forest onto Cougar Divide ridge crest (Trail #601), ~1,790 ft gain to ~5,920 ft
Cross-country along Cougar Divide ridge to the Chowder Ridge junction; broad open ridge with occasional loose sections
Chowder Ridge traverse north on an established boot-path; mild exposure, side-hilling on steep slope
Final northwest-ridge summit block; loose rock, hard class 3 scrambling to the small, exposed summit

approach_variants.name: Cougar Divide Trail #601 and the open ridge northeast to Chowder Ridge
approach_variants.notes:
From Glacier, WA, drive SR-542 east and turn onto Forest Service Road 33; follow about 11 miles of gravel — rough in sections, high-clearance recommended, sedans passable with care — to its end at the Cougar Divide trailhead, with room for eight to ten vehicles. The true trailhead may be roughly a kilometre past where online mapping routes you, so do not stop at the first turnaround that looks right.

Hike Cougar Divide Trail #601 along the ridge to its high point around 5,920 ft. That high point is where maintained tread ends and the route becomes cross-country: continue northeast along the open ridge, crossing near Dobbs Creek, to Chowder Ridge and the foot of Hadley's summit block.

This and the Skyline Divide route are two different walks to the SAME summit block; the beta below for the block is common to both.
approach_variants.season: Roughly Aug-Oct, once the ridge is out from under snow
hazards: Eleven miles of rough gravel road, and a trailhead that mapping apps place short of the real one
Cross-country ridge travel with no tread and no cairns once past the 5,920 ft high point
Loose scree below a short Class 3 step
Open ridge with no shelter and no water beyond the trailhead
In cloud, two different divides converge on this summit and neither exit is marked
approach_variants.baseFinding:
THE RIDGE IS THE ROUTE AND ITS HIGH POINT IS THE HANDOFF. Trail #601 runs along the crest to a high point near 5,920 ft, and everything after that is open ridge. In cloud you do not need a view: stay on the crest, going northeast, with the ground falling away on both sides. The moment you are sidehilling with the drop on only one side, you have come off the divide.

ARRIVAL AT THE CLIMBING, and this is the test that matters: the summit block of Hadley is a SHORT CLASS 3 STEP above loose scree, roughly the last 100 ft of the day. Everything below it is walking. So the base is the point where the ridge stops being walkable and stands up in a single short step. If you are scrambling for hundreds of feet you are on the wrong feature; if you have not scrambled at all you are not at the summit.

THE APPROACH IS NOT A LOOP AND CHOWDER RIDGE IS THE CONFIRMATION. You should arrive at the block having travelled along Chowder Ridge. If you are dropping into a basin or crossing a glacier to reach a rock block, you are somewhere else on the north side of Baker.

WHICH DIVIDE DID YOU WALK IN ON? This is the one thing to be sure of before you commit to a descent line in poor visibility, because the two approaches to this summit leave in different directions and neither is signed. Cougar Divide comes in from the NORTH-WEST via Dobbs Creek; Skyline Divide comes in from the WEST along a much longer open ridge. Note your entry point onto Chowder Ridge on the way up.

before.beta: From the Cougar Divide Trailhead (~4,900 ft), the maintained Cougar Divide Trail #601 climbs along a ridge crest through meadows and old growth to its high point near 5,920 ft (about 3.1 miles in). From there the route continues cross-country along the open ridge, crossing toward Dobbs Cleaver/Chowder Ridge, to merge with the Skyline Divide approach below Hadley Peak's northwest ridge. The final push to the summit is Class 2 with a brief Class 3 step over loose scree, with generally mild exposure for experienced scramblers.
before.descent: Reverse the ascent line: downclimb the loose summit scramble, retrace the ridge back to the Cougar Divide Trail high point, and follow the maintained trail back to the trailhead.
before.descent_text: From the summit, downclimb the short Class 3 step and loose scree back onto the connecting ridge, then retrace the cross-country ridge traverse back to the Cougar Divide Trail's high point (~5,920 ft). Follow the maintained Cougar Divide Trail #601 back down through meadows and forest to the trailhead.

climate.fall: Generally the best window (mid-August to early October) — drier trail, fewer bugs, but earliest season snow possible by late October.
climate.spring: Road gate still closed (opens July 7); ridge typically snow-covered regardless.
climate.summer: Prime season once the road gate opens in July; heather/meadow terrain usually dry by August, mosquitoes can be heavy into July.
climate.winter: Road gated and route not accessible in standard scramble form.
climate.typical: Wet, maritime North Cascades weather with rapid changes possible even in summer; the higher trailhead means less low-elevation approach but similar exposed-ridge weather near the summit.
climate.forecastZone: NWAC West Slopes North (Mount Baker area)
